messages:
Zoe: Quick WFH chaos report + tiny DIY brag. Turned an old ironing board into a standing desk this weekend. Works great except the router ended up on the floor and my cat thinks it's a hockey puck. Live demo photo: https://images.redwood.example/zoe-ironing-desk-2026.jpg :cat:

Ethan: lol. Cat + router is a classic. Any signs of packet loss or just random lag?

Zoe: Random lag, occasional freeze during calls. Not sure if it's interference or the router being too low.

Priya: Run a quick ping while you're on a call to check jitter/packet loss. Example I use when troubleshooting:

Priya: ```
$ ping -c 6 1.1.1.1
PING 1.1.1.1 (1.1.1.1): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=1 ttl=57 time=9.2 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=2 ttl=57 time=78.4 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=3 ttl=57 time=11.0 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=4 ttl=57 time=10.8 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=5 ttl=57 time=130.7 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=6 ttl=57 time=10.6 ms
--- 1.1.1.1 ping statistics ---
6 packets transmitted, 6 packets received, 0% packet loss
round-trip min/avg/max = 9.2/41.8/130.7 ms
```

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: observed zoe-laptop 3 retransmits during 30m window starting 1768581305; peak RTT 142ms; suggested action: elevate AP >30cm, avoid metal near antenna, or use 5GHz band.

Maya: If you want a temporary fix, a USB extension + dongle up on the shelf worked for me. Also consider a little rubber mat under the router if the cat keeps sliding it around.

Ethan: Debate time: mesh vs single stronger AP vs powerline. Mesh wins if your place has thick walls, single AP + repositioning if it's just height. Powerline is a nostalgia move but can work if wiring is decent.

Zoe: Poll: reaction with :chair: if you vote "keep the ironing board", :hammer: if you vote "duct-tape cat to ottoman" (kidding), :package: for "buy a small mesh node". GIFs accepted.

Priya: Also check the router's admin page for channel congestion. If neighbors are on the same 2.4GHz channel, that explains hiccups. Switch to an uncongested 5GHz channel if available.

Zoe: Did the USB-dongle trick — plug it onto a 1m extension and perched it on the bookshelf. No more dropouts during a 45m call. Cat is sulking because its puck moved. Victory pic: https://images.redwood.example/zoe-router-victory.jpg :tada:

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: zoe-laptop events cleared at 1768581498; no retransmits in last 20m. Marking as resolved.

Maya: Bonus tip: If you leave the ironing board up all week, put a non-slip bump on the feet otherwise the cat will push it mid-standup.

Zoe: Thanks all! New standing desk, happier calls, and one disgruntled cat. Will accept duct-tape memes in thread.
